reasons: R04, R14, R09, R17: sales grew roughly 14.6x in one year (cash sales up 13.7x); M-score 6.83 and F-score 9.55 are far above thresholds, though both are pushed up mainly by SGI on what is likely a small base
F12, F13: one customer is 51% of revenue and 65% of receivables, so a single counterparty dominates the revenue and the receivables to be collected
F11, F22: material related-party transactions alongside a major acquisition in the year make it possible that revenue or asset values come from transactions that are not at arm's length
F24, F10: the auditor flagged revenue as a critical audit matter, and the company discloses return rights or bill-and-hold arrangements, which are classic areas for revenue to be recognised too early
R13, R03: soft assets make up 99% of total assets (intangibles/goodwill/IP), so the balance sheet rests on judgemental valuations that may need impairment
R02, R15: gross margin index 0.18 means a sharp margin improvement, and ROA swung strongly, both in step with the jump in revenue. That fits high-margin licensing-type revenue that is hard to verify
F21, R16, R07, F20: capital raised in the year, securities issued, leverage index 2.39 and incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS all give management pressure and motive to report growth

R19, R08, R10, R18, R11: operating cash flow covers only 0.3x net income, but accruals are negative and receivables did not grow faster than sales, which partly offsets concerns about aggressive accruals

F01, F03, F04, F05, F07, F16, F17: no material weakness, no going concern, no auditor change, no restatement, and no SEC inquiry or class action disclosed. However, ICFR is not audited (F03), so the clean control assessment gives limited comfort
